lesson.concept: Before you can compare exponents, both sides must be written as powers of the SAME base. 3^x = 27 is not solved by comparing 3 and 27. Rewrite 27 as 3^3.
lesson.why: This is one of the highest-frequency errors DBE reported for this section.

work: Step 1: rewrite 27 as a power of 3. 27 = 3^3.
Step 3: same base, equate exponents: x = 3
Do not write x = 27/3. That treats it like linear algebra.

probe.hint: See the example for the pattern.

learner_message: Both sides must be written as powers of the same base before the exponents can be equated.
